kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Upper band Rs 700. At Rs 700: market cap Rs 4,009.75 cr, P/E 78.8x FY26 diluted EPS Rs 8.88, P/B 7.25x, EV/EBITDA 39.1x FY26. Institutions bought from CEAQ at Rs 700 on 29-30 Sep 2026 (pp. 151-152).

focus.title: Cash flow vs profit
focus.detail: Operating cash flow Rs 783.33 m in FY24, then -1,361.19 m (FY25, incl. the final instalments for the IP purchase) and -632.16 m (FY26) as export orders were deferred and stock was built for FY27 orders (pp. 23, 25, 439). Cumulative CFO/PAT FY24-26 -63.0%. A timing item in a lumpy order cycle; track H1 FY27 cash flow.

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Disclosed related-party dealings with CEAQ Singapore (former parent): the one-time IP purchase of Rs 1,831.91 m in FY24, valued by DCF and paid in instalments, which removed future royalties; and material purchases of Rs 789.80 m in FY26 (26.3% of total expenses). Track the share of purchases from CEAQ after listing.

focus.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
focus.detail: No goodwill. Intangible assets Rs 1,627.01 m at 31-Mar-2026 = 29.4% of net worth, mostly the related-party IP purchase; amortisation lifts D&A from Rs 133.95 m (FY24) to Rs 313.35 m (FY26).

focus.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
focus.detail: Top-10 customers 77.83% of FY26 revenue and 98.17% in Q1 FY27 (top-1 54.74%); Indian Government 71.19% of FY26 revenue; foreign-government revenue fell from Rs 2,676.93 m to Rs 121.14 m. Top-10 suppliers 68.77% of FY26 total expenses with no long-term supply contracts.

focus.title: Contingent liabilities
focus.detail: Bank guarantees Rs 789.34 m = 14.7% of 30-Jun-2026 net worth; GST disputes Rs 8.32 m; a customs notice received 23-Jul-2026 is disclosed as a contingent liability without an amount. Materiality threshold Rs 32.03 m (p. 447).

focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -88.5% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

bankers.owner: Promoted by the Kampani family: J M Financial & Investment Consultancy Services Pvt Ltd 24.77%, Nimesh Kampani 13.11%, J M Assets Management Pvt Ltd 11.36%, Aruna Kampani 2.82%, SNK Investments 1.95%, Vishal Kampani 1.36%; promoter group about 57% (June 2026)

bankers.name: IIFL Capital Services Limited
bankers.owner: Promoter group led by the IIFL founders; shareholding percentages not sourced in this run
bankers.listed: Yes (formerly IIFL Securities Limited) - listing status per secondary sources, unverified

issues.issuer: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd

strengths: 100% ownership of IP since Mar-2024 across optics, IR engines and video processing (pp. 138, 246)
Largest supplier of thermal imaging systems to Indian government agencies Apr-24 to Mar-26; 94% of Indian thermal-imaging exports by units FY24-26 (issuer-paid F&S report, p. 246)
28,000+ systems deployed in 24 countries; ITAR-free portfolio (p. 246)
Cash tax 23.3% of cumulative FY24-26 PBT; no auditor qualifications or auditor change (pp. 89, 100, 440)
weaknesses: FY26 revenue Rs 362.65 cr, down 22.69%, as export orders slipped; Q1 FY27 is seasonally small (Rs 36.01 cr) (pp. 23, 89)
Working capital 109.7% of FY26 revenue; cumulative CFO -Rs 121.00 cr FY24-26 (pp. 87, 90)
Top-10 customers 77.83% of FY26 revenue, typical of defence tendering (p. 24)
Materials from related party CEAQ Singapore 26.3% of FY26 expenses (p. 94)
Inventory Rs 319.63 cr at Jun-26 built ahead of FY27 deliveries (pp. 25, 87)
opportunities: India EO/IR market $522 m (CY2020) to $1.4 bn (CY2030), 10.5% CAGR - issuer-paid F&S report (p. 205)
Orders of Rs 118.15 cr received Jul-Sep 2026, incl. a Rs 51.44 cr export order deferred from FY26 (pp. 23, 250)
Platform systems grew from Rs 12.70 cr (FY24) to Rs 144.81 cr (FY26) (p. 248)
IDDM eligibility under DAP 2020 favours indigenous OEMs (p. 247)
threats: Tender-based, non-recurring contracts; bid-win ratio 14.29% in Q1 FY27 vs 40.91% in FY24 (p. 23)
Export orders exposed to conflicts and export approvals: foreign-government revenue Rs 267.69 cr -> Rs 12.11 cr FY25-26 (p. 251)
Singapore High Court suit by a CEAQ Singapore minority shareholder naming the company, MD and a nominee director (p. 448)
Lock-in expiries: 287 lakh pre-issue shares (50% of capital) free after six months (p. 121)

adjustments.item: Warranty provision written back to profit
adjustments.reason: FY26 other expenses include a Rs 18.84 cr write-back of warranty provisions 'of earlier years'; FY24 and FY25 carried charges of Rs 20.82 cr and Rs 8.15 cr, so the release flatters FY26 alone (a further Rs 5.98 cr was written back in Q1 FY27).

adjustments.item: Development spending capitalised instead of expensed (net of software amortisation)
adjustments.reason: Additions to software and intangible CWIP rose to Rs 34.17 cr in FY26 from Rs 5.06 cr (FY25) and Rs 1.40 cr (FY24, excl. the IP purchase); the policy capitalises R&D staff costs and consultancy. Allowed under Ind AS 38 when its tests are met; shown expensed, less software amortisation of Rs 6.67 cr. The RHP does not split purchased licences from in-house development.

adjustments.item: Amortisation of the IP bought from CEAQ Singapore (non-cash)
adjustments.reason: Raises earnings: the Rs 183.19 cr IP purchase is amortised over 10 years (Rs 18.32 cr a year) and replaced royalty payments. Shown for balance; not in the adjusted P/E.

adjustments.item: Executive pay at the contracted rates from Dec-2025
adjustments.reason: Contracted pay of about Rs 7.66 cr a year against Rs 5.21 cr drawn in FY26: a run-rate item for FY27, not an accounting choice.

adjustments.item: Other income (mainly interest on term deposits)
adjustments.reason: Recurring while the deposits are held, but not from operations; excluding it gives the operating P/E.

earnings_quality.verdict: Reported FY26 P/E of 78.8x is flattered by the items flagged: adjusted P/E 247.5x (PAT -68.2%). On the FY24-FY26 average, which smooths one-year items, the P/E is 62.6x reported and 75.6x adjusted.
flags: FY26 other expenses include a Rs 18.84 cr write-back of warranty provisions 'of earlier years'; FY24 and FY25 carried charges of Rs 20.82 cr and Rs 8.15 cr, so the release flatters FY26 alone (a further Rs 5.98 cr was written back in Q1 FY27).

Additions to software and intangible CWIP rose to Rs 34.17 cr in FY26 from Rs 5.06 cr (FY25) and Rs 1.40 cr (FY24, excl. the IP purchase); the policy capitalises R&D staff costs and consultancy. Allowed under Ind AS 38 when its tests are met; shown expensed, less software amortisation of Rs 6.67 cr. The RHP does not split purchased licences from in-house development.
checked: Employee stock option cost charged to profit (Rs 12.28 cr in FY26) (p. 90)
No change in depreciation or amortisation policy: IP over 10 years, software over 3-5 years (p. 342)
No borrowing costs disclosed as capitalised (pp. 342, 351)
Profit taxed in cash: current tax 23.3% of cumulative PBT; deferred tax small (p. 89)
No exceptional gains: exceptional items were charges of Rs 0.78 cr (FY25) and Rs 0.41 cr (FY24) (p. 89)
Bad debts written off through profit: Rs 21.82 cr, Rs 19.05 cr and Rs 3.35 cr FY24-26 (p. 373)
No auditor qualification or emphasis of matter (p. 440)
